topic.name: Properties of Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y

question.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y= 3$ and $\displaystyle\int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y= 5,$ calculate $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y$ given that $C = C_1\cup C_2.$
question.explanation:
Let $C = C_1\cup C_2$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation.

For line integrals with respect to $y,$ we have the following properties:

  • $\displaystyle\int_{-C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d y = -\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d y$

  • $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d y = \int_{C_1} f(x,y)\,\textrm d y + \int_{C_2} f(x,y)\,\textrm d y$

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} \int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y &= \int_{C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y + \int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= - \int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y + \int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= -3 + 5\\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

question.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= -1$ and $\displaystyle\int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= 4,$ calculate $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x$ given that $C = C_1\cup C_2.$
question.explanation:
Let $C = C_1\cup C_2$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation.

For line integrals with respect to $x,$ we have the following properties:

  • $\displaystyle\int_{-C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = -\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

  • $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = \int_{C_1} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} \int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x &= \int_{C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x \\[5pt] &= -\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x - \int_{-C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x \\[5pt] &= -(-1) - 4\\[5pt] &= -3. \end{align*}

question.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= 14$ and $\displaystyle\int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x= 10,$ calculate $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x$ given that $C = C_1\cup C_2.$
question.explanation:
Let $C = C_1\cup C_2$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation.

For line integrals with respect to $x,$ we have the following properties:

  • $\displaystyle\int_{-C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = -\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

  • $\displaystyle\int_{C} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x = \int_{C_1} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y)\,\textrm d x$

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} \int_{C} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x &= \int_{C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x \\[5pt] &= -\int_{-C_1} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x + \int_{C_2} f(x,y) \,\textrm d x \\[5pt] &= -14 + 10\\[5pt] &= -4. \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle\oint_C \,\textrm d y,$ where $C=C_1 \cup C_2\cup C_3$ is the path comprising of two line segments and a semicircle or radius $4,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, as shown above.
question.explanation:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

\[ \oint_C \,\textrm d y = y_2 - y_1, \] where $y_2$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and $y_1$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, $y_1 = y_2,$ and we have

\[ \oint_C \,\textrm d y = 0. \]
